To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the buckling stress of the stiffened panel is significantly influenced by the geometrical dimensions of the stiffened web and the localized initial imperfection, and the effect of the imperfection depends on the geometrical configuration of the stiffener web.

The buckling strength of a stiffened plate is significantly affected by the presence of a single localized initial defect, which is characterized by the defect depth, the defect width, the defect location, the defect orientation and the defect symmetry.

the main parameters that influence the buckling strength of a perfect stiffened plate are the plate and the web width, and the main parameters that control the buckling strength when a single localized defect is present are the defect depth and the defect width.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the assessment of the bucking stress of stiffened plates under in-plane uniform compression.
the buckling limit states of imperfect stiffened panels under axial compression, which is a fundamental problem in engineering.
the assessment of buckling limit states in stiffened plates made of an elastic homogeneous and an isotropic material.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the buckling strength of a stiffened plate is mainly controlled by the plate width, followed by the web height, and finally the plate length.
the buckling strength is a complex function of the geometrical parameters of the plate and of the defect characteristics, with a clear dominance of the defect depth.

the main parameters governing the buckling stress of the perfect plate are plate width a, then web height b, then web width t, then finally the combined interaction between plate width and web height b, and between web width and web height.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

buckling strength of the stiffened plates is highly sensitive to the geometrical dimensions of the panel, as well as to the localized initial geometric imperfetions, which are characterized by their amplitude, length, and width.
the buckling limit stress of a perfect stiffened plate is a function of the plate width, the web height and the web width.
the buckling limit stress is a function of the geometric parameters and of the initial defect parameters.
